classification.difficultyReason: Students identify the sectors making angle AOB and either add them or subtract the other sectors from a straight angle or revolution. These are direct applications of the taught angle totals.

content.prompt: Find the size of $\angle AOB$ in each diagram below.

spec.description: Horizontal straight line through O, with OB rightwards and two upper rays. OA is the upper-right ray.
spec.mathematics: Successive angles above the straight line are 35 degrees, 100 degrees and the requested angle AOB.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle AOB+35^\circ+100^\circ&=180^\circ\\\angle AOB&=180^\circ-135^\circ\\\angle AOB&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
Reason: straight angle at $O$.

spec.description: Five rays fan upwards from O, with OB leftmost and OA rightmost.
spec.mathematics: From OB towards OA, adjacent sectors are 33, 28, 29 and 30 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: All four givens remain visible; their sum is absent.

spec.description: Four rays around O, with three marked sectors and the unmarked sector between OA and OB. Opposing rays are not assumed collinear.
spec.mathematics: Clockwise from OA, supplied sectors are 120, 85 and 89 degrees; the remaining sector is AOB.
spec.answerVisibility: The requested sector has no supplied value.

answer.short:
$66^\circ$

Subtract the three known sectors from a revolution.

spec.description: OA upper-left, a vertical ray upwards and OB upper-right, with adjacent marked sectors.
spec.mathematics: AOV is 40 degrees and VOB is 60 degrees, where V denotes the unlabelled vertical ray only in the editable construction.
spec.answerVisibility: Only A, O and B are printed as point labels; the requested sum is absent.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle AOB&=40^\circ+60^\circ\\\angle AOB&=100^\circ\end{align*}$$
Reason: adjacent angles at $O$.
